clips.title: Frozen goods temperature check
clips.transcript: A refrigerated truck arrives. The receiving associate checks the frozen cartons with a temperature probe before accepting the shipment.
clips.description: A frozen-food delivery arrives for restaurant supply. The learner must notice that temperature is checked before acceptance.
clips.expectedObservation: Frozen goods must be temperature-checked before acceptance.
clips.expectedDecision: Hold acceptance until cold-chain condition is verified and escalate if outside limits.
clips.lessonContent: Frozen products can become unsafe if the cold chain is broken. The first receiving action is to verify temperature and condition before the cartons enter normal stock flow.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should the associate check before accepting frozen goods?

answerOptions.label: Product temperature and cold-chain condition
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Temperature and cold-chain condition decide whether frozen goods can be accepted.

answerOptions.label: Carton colour
answerOptions.feedback: Carton colour is not the safety control. Temperature and condition come first.

answerOptions.label: Driver name
answerOptions.feedback: Driver identity may matter administratively, but it does not replace cold-chain verification.

clips.title: Wrong supplier at receiving
clips.transcript: The associate compares the delivery note with carton labels and notices the supplier name does not match the expected delivery.
clips.description: A delivery arrives with a supplier mismatch. The learner must catch it before counting or inspection effort is spent.
clips.expectedObservation: Supplier identity on cartons does not match the delivery note or purchase order.
clips.expectedDecision: Reject or hold the delivery at the dock and notify the supervisor before unloading continues.
clips.lessonContent: A wrong-supplier delivery is caught at the earliest receiving step. Continuing to count or inspect the wrong shipment wastes effort and risks accepting stock that should never enter the dock flow.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is the safest next action when supplier identity does not match?

answerOptions.label: Stop unloading, reject or hold, and escalate
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Supplier mismatch is a dock-level stop condition.

answerOptions.label: Continue counting first
answerOptions.feedback: Counting should not continue when the delivery identity itself is wrong.

answerOptions.label: Accept now and fix paperwork later
answerOptions.feedback: That creates a serious receiving control failure.

clips.title: FNV damage segregation
clips.transcript: A quality associate checks tomatoes and leafy greens, finds visible damage, and moves one crate aside for quality hold.
clips.description: Fresh produce is inspected for visible spoilage, bruising, excess moisture, and freshness before acceptance.
clips.expectedObservation: One FNV crate has visible quality damage and should not flow into accepted stock.
clips.expectedDecision: Separate the damaged crate and record it for quality hold or supervisor review.
clips.lessonContent: FNV quality issues must be separated at inspection. Mixing damaged stock with accepted crates can affect restaurant order quality and food safety.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should be done with the damaged FNV crate?

answerOptions.label: Move it aside for quality hold
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Damaged produce should be segregated and recorded.

answerOptions.label: Mix it with accepted crates
answerOptions.feedback: Mixing damaged stock hides the issue and weakens quality control.

answerOptions.label: Ignore it if only one crate is affected
answerOptions.feedback: Small exceptions still need to be recorded and controlled.

clips.title: Chilled dairy immediate put-away
clips.transcript: The associate scans dairy crates and moves them quickly from receiving into a chilled room instead of leaving them at ambient temperature.
clips.description: Chilled dairy products are transferred into cold storage without unnecessary dwell time.
clips.expectedObservation: Dairy stock should not remain in the ambient receiving area.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan and move dairy crates into chilled storage promptly.
clips.lessonContent: Chilled dairy has a narrow handling window. The correct process is to scan, verify, and move it to the chilled zone quickly while preserving traceability.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What is the priority after chilled dairy is verified?

answerOptions.label: Move it to chilled storage promptly
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Chilled dairy should not dwell at ambient temperature.

answerOptions.label: Leave it at the dock until all goods are received
answerOptions.feedback: That increases cold-chain risk.

answerOptions.label: Store it in ambient racks temporarily
answerOptions.feedback: Dairy must go to the correct chilled zone.

clips.title: Ambient staples location scan
clips.transcript: The associate scans a carton of staples, then scans the rack location label before placing it in the ambient storage bay.
clips.description: Ambient staples such as rice, flour, pulses, spices, and oil cans are placed only after product and location scans.
clips.expectedObservation: Both item barcode and rack location must be scanned to prevent inventory mismatch.
clips.expectedDecision: Scan product and location before completing put-away.
clips.lessonContent: Location accuracy matters as much as physical movement. A missed rack scan can make stock unavailable for restaurant orders even when it is physically present.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Which scans are required before put-away is completed?

answerOptions.label: Product barcode and rack location
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Both scans preserve inventory accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Product barcode only
answerOptions.feedback: Product-only scanning does not prove the item reached the right bin.

answerOptions.label: Rack location only
answerOptions.feedback: Location-only scanning does not prove which stock was placed.

clips.title: Restaurant order route loading
clips.transcript: A dispatch executive checks route totes for a hotel, a restaurant, and a cafe before loading them into the correct vehicle bay.
clips.description: Mixed customer orders are loaded by route and customer sequence to avoid wrong deliveries.
clips.expectedObservation: Totes must match route/customer labels before loading.
clips.expectedDecision: Verify route sequence and load only the correct totes into the assigned vehicle.
clips.lessonContent: Hotels, restaurants, and cafes depend on accurate route loading. A tote placed in the wrong vehicle can create a missed delivery even if picking was correct.
clips.assessmentQuestion: What should be checked before route loading?

answerOptions.label: Route and customer labels match the vehicle bay
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Route/customer match prevents wrong delivery.

answerOptions.label: Only the box weight
answerOptions.feedback: Weight does not confirm route or customer accuracy.

answerOptions.label: Load whatever is closest first
answerOptions.feedback: Speed cannot override route control.

clips.title: Returned goods quarantine
clips.transcript: A returned carton from a restaurant delivery is placed in a quarantine area while the supervisor checks the return reason and condition.
clips.description: Returned food-service goods are separated from saleable stock until disposition is approved.
clips.expectedObservation: Returned goods must not be mixed back into available inventory without review.
clips.expectedDecision: Move returns to quarantine and wait for supervisor disposition.
clips.lessonContent: Returns may have unknown handling history. Quarantine protects customers and inventory accuracy until the approved disposition is recorded.
clips.assessmentQuestion: Where should returned goods go before approval?

answerOptions.label: Quarantine area
answerOptions.feedback: Correct. Returned goods require controlled review before disposition.

answerOptions.label: Available stock rack
answerOptions.feedback: Returned goods cannot be mixed into available stock without review.

answerOptions.label: Nearest empty space
answerOptions.feedback: Returns need controlled quarantine, not convenience storage.
